answer: A commit-reveal bond stops one operator farming many identities from one job. Each epoch, an identity stakes 40 credits and files a quill-signed commit, a hash of work only it can reveal. It must present its pearl, a task receipt bound to that commit; a pearl shown under two commits forfeits the stake. The k-th fake needs a k-th task and a k-th 40-credit stake, so 1,000 fakes cost 40,000 credits plus 1,000 tasks, while an honest agent pays 40 once and keeps its share. Proof rental fails since a rented pearl matches its original commit, and the voyage cannot be copied.
